steps.title: Sterilize pestles and label tubes
steps.instruction: Wash eppendorf‑size pestles, rinse with 100 % ethanol then distilled water, autoclave; label three sets of 1.5 ml eppendorf tubes. Up to 42 samples (two people) can be processed in one day.

steps.title: Prepare 2X CTAB extraction buffer
steps.instruction: For 500 ml buffer: dissolve 10 g NaCl (≈1.4 M) and add 140 ml of 5 M NaCl; add 20 ml of 0.5 M EDTA (20 mM); add 10 ml of 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 8.0 (100 mM); fill to 500 ml with water and adjust pH to 8.0.

steps.title: Aliquot CTAB buffer with additives
steps.instruction: For each extraction aliquot prepare 600 µl of CTAB solution; optionally add 1 % (w/v) PVP just before use and incubate at 65 °C to dissolve; immediately before adding to tissue add 6 µl β‑mercaptoethanol and 12 µl of 0.5 M EDTA pH 8.0 per 600 µl CTAB.

steps.title: Weigh and grind plant material
steps.instruction: Weigh ~100 mg fresh tissue, 20–30 mg silica‑dried tissue, or ≥ two 6 cm herbarium leaves; place tissue on wax paper, crush, transfer to a clean eppendorf, add a small amount of liquid nitrogen and grind to a fine powder.

steps.title: Add CTAB buffer and homogenize
steps.instruction: Add 300 µl of the prepared CTAB‑mercaptoethanol‑EDTA‑PVP buffer to the powder, homogenize; add a further 300 µl of the same buffer and homogenize well (total 600 µl).

steps.title: Add RNAse A and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 2 µl RNAse A (10 mg ml⁻¹) per tube (RNAse can be added directly to the CTAB solution). Incubate tubes in a 65 °C water bath for 30 min, mixing 2–3 times during incubation.

steps.title: First chloroform‑isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Add 1 volume (600 µl) chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (24:1), invert gently for 10 min; centrifuge at maximum microcentrifuge speed for 15 min; transfer the upper aqueous layer to a second set of pre‑labelled tubes, avoiding the interphase debris.

steps.title: Second chloroform‑isoamyl extraction
steps.instruction: Add another 600 µl chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (24:1), invert ~5 min; centrifuge at maximum speed for 15 min; transfer the top layer to a third set of tubes.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with cold ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 1 ml ice‑cold 100 % ethanol (≈2 volumes) to each tube, invert to mix. Incubate at room temperature for 30 min to 2 h (if a large pellet is visible, 15–30 min is sufficient). Optional: use 1.5 volumes of isopropanol instead; ethanol works best for Carex and roses.

steps.title: Pellet DNA and wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at maximum speed for 20 min; pour off ethanol, leaving the visible pellet. Add 1 ml room‑temperature Wash Buffer (76 % ethanol, 10 mM ammonium acetate), dislodge pellet, and let sit on a low‑speed shaker for at least 1 h. Centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 min; discard wash buffer and remove residual liquid by tapping and blotting.

steps.title: Dry and resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Air‑dry open tubes under a hood for ~1 h until no alcohol odor is detectable (or dry‑vacuum for 4–6 min). Resuspend pellet in 150 µl TE (10 mM Tris‑HCl, 1 mM EDTA, pH 7.4) or distilled water; pipette TE over the pellet, tap to aid dissolution, then incubate at 65 °C for 10 min, tapping occasionally.

steps.title: Optional post‑extraction RNAse treatment
steps.instruction: If RNAse was not added earlier, add 2 µl RNAse A (10 mg ml⁻¹) and incubate 30 min at 37 °C water bath; add 20 µl chloroform‑isoamyl alcohol (24:1), invert gently; centrifuge 5 min at maximum speed; transfer the aqueous layer to a new tube. DNA is now ready for PCR.

steps.title: Aliquot and store DNA
steps.instruction: Optionally divide the DNA into aliquots; store one at –20 °C and another at –80 °C for long‑term storage. For frequent PCR within a week, keep DNA at 4 °C; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles which shear DNA.
